definition: Matching the same person across non-overlapping camera views using appearance embeddings.
details: Matching the same person across non-overlapping camera views using appearance embeddings. It is essential for multi-camera tracking and video surveillance analytics.

explainer.lead: Person re-identification matches the same person across non-overlapping camera views using appearance embeddings. It is essential for multi-camera tracking and video surveillance analytics.

tiers.eli5: When someone walks out of one camera's view and into another's, this is how the system knows it is still the same person.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build appearance embeddings so the same person's images from different, non-overlapping cameras can be matched, supporting multi-camera tracking and surveillance analytics.
tiers.paperLevel: Matching the same person across non-overlapping camera views using appearance embeddings; essential for multi-camera tracking and video surveillance analytics.

explainer.example: A person seen by one street camera is matched, via their appearance embedding, to images of the same person captured later by a different camera with no overlapping view.
